# ref_txn

Moves 1 to 64 refs as one operation, each by compare-and-swap, all of them or none: each move names its ref, expect (the full 64-hex changeset id it holds when you read it; omitted to create it) and to (omitted to delete it). Every expectation is checked first: any stale one is E\_CAS\_MISMATCH, every failed ref in details.mismatches, nothing written. undo of its id restores every ref at once.

```yaml
title: "ref_txn"
description: "Move several refs at once."
since: "0.1.0"
mutates: true
identity_required: true
cli_command: "swarmops ref txn"
envelope_op: "ref_txn"
request_type: "RefTxnReq"
annotations: {"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":false}
max_result_chars: null
```

## Input schema

`arguments` is a `RefTxnReq`: `swarmops schema RefTxnReq` prints the type. A field the type does not know is ignored.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `moves` | array of object | yes |  | The moves: 1 to 64 (`E_INVALID_ARG` for none, `E_TOO_LARGE` past 64), each ref once. |

### JSON Schema

As `tools/list` gives it: each `$ref` replaced by its definition, so that it stands alone.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "description": "`ref_txn` (CLI `ref txn`): move several refs as one operation, each by compare-and-swap, all\nof them or none. Every expectation is checked under the store's lock\nbefore any move is made: one or more that fail make it `E_CAS_MISMATCH`, every failed ref in\n`details.mismatches`, and nothing is written. Each move follows `ref set`'s and `ref\ndelete`'s rules: `main` only along its first parents and never deleted (`E_REF_PROTECTED`), a\ntag never moved (`E_TAG_IMMUTABLE`), no remote-tracking ref (`E_REF_NAME_INVALID`).",
  "properties": {
    "moves": {
      "description": "The moves: 1 to 64 (`E_INVALID_ARG` for none, `E_TOO_LARGE` past 64), each ref once.",
      "items": {
        "description": "One move of a `ref_txn`: ref `name` from `expect` to `to`. A move that changes nothing\n(`expect` and `to` the same, or both omitted) is `E_INVALID_ARG`.",
        "properties": {
          "expect": {
            "anyOf": [
              {
                "pattern": "^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$",
                "type": "string"
              },
              {
                "type": "null"
              }
            ],
            "description": "The target the caller last saw, by its full changeset id, as `ref set`'s `expected_old`;\nomitted to create the ref, which must not exist."
          },
          "name": {
            "description": "The ref: `main`, `release/<name>` or a tag.",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "to": {
            "anyOf": [
              {
                "description": "A revision as the caller wrote it, for the store to resolve: a ref name (`main`,\n`release/1.2`), a full 64-hex changeset id or a unique prefix of at least 12 hex digits, or a\nref's earlier value: `<ref>@{N}` the value it held N moves before its current one (`@{0}`\nis the current value), `<ref>@{at=<unix seconds>}` the value set by its newest move\nrecorded at or before that instant (the writer's clock, moves read in journal order);\noptionally followed by `~N` for the N-th first-parent ancestor.",
                "type": "string"
              },
              {
                "type": "null"
              }
            ],
            "description": "The revision to point it at; omitted to delete it."
          }
        },
        "required": [
          "name"
        ],
        "type": "object"
      },
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "moves"
  ],
  "title": "RefTxnReq",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## Annotations

It moves or deletes refs by compare-and-swap, changing what they name. Run again with the same arguments, it finds them as it asked (`already_applied`) or not as it expected (`E_CAS_MISMATCH`), and changes nothing more.

| Annotation | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `destructiveHint` | `true` | True: a tool that changes the store may overwrite or delete what is there, not only add to it. |
| `idempotentHint` | `true` | True: calling it again with the same arguments changes nothing more. |
| `openWorldHint` | `false` | True: it reaches beyond a closed set of things. Every tool here stays inside the store. |
| `readOnlyHint` | `false` | True: the tool does not change its environment, the store. |

Its entry in `tools/list` carries no `_meta`.

## CLI command

[`swarmops ref txn`](../commands/ref-txn.md) runs the same operation and prints the same envelope.

## Examples

### MCP

```json
{
  "id": 45,
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "arguments": {
      "moves": [
        {
          "name": "release/a",
          "to": "[c1]"
        },
        {
          "name": "release/b",
          "to": "[c1]"
        }
      ]
    },
    "name": "ref_txn"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "id": 45,
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "text": "{\"api\":1,\"meta\":{\"auth\":\"trust\",\"elapsed_ms\":\"[elapsed_ms]\",\"repo\":\"[tmp]/store\",\"resolved\":{\"[c1]\":\"[c1]\"}},\"ok\":true,\"op\":\"ref_txn\",\"result\":{\"id\":\"18:[crc]\",\"moves\":[{\"actor\":\"agent/worker-17\",\"at\":\"[at]\",\"name\":\"release/a\",\"new\":\"[c1]\"},{\"actor\":\"agent/worker-17\",\"at\":\"[at]\",\"name\":\"release/b\",\"new\":\"[c1]\"}],\"op\":18}}",
        "type": "text"
      }
    ],
    "isError": false,
    "structuredContent": {
      "api": 1,
      "meta": {
        "auth": "trust",
        "elapsed_ms": "[elapsed_ms]",
        "repo": "[tmp]/store",
        "resolved": {
          "[c1]": "[c1]"
        }
      },
      "ok": true,
      "op": "ref_txn",
      "result": {
        "id": "18:[crc]",
        "moves": [
          {
            "actor": "agent/worker-17",
            "at": "[at]",
            "name": "release/a",
            "new": "[c1]"
          },
          {
            "actor": "agent/worker-17",
            "at": "[at]",
            "name": "release/b",
            "new": "[c1]"
          }
        ],
        "op": 18
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The server ran as `swarmops mcp --repo [tmp]/store --as agent/worker-17`, after `initialize`. Recorded by the MCP tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time, the version.

## Return information

A tool result: the envelope, whose `op` is `ref_txn`, as `structuredContent` and again as the text of its one `content` block. `isError` is true exactly when the envelope's `ok` is false. On success the envelope's `result` is what [`swarmops ref txn`](../commands/ref-txn.md#return-information) returns.

## Errors

A failed call is a tool result with `isError: true`; the envelope's `error.code` is one of the [error codes](../errors.md).

- [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg): arguments that do not fit `RefTxnReq`, a field named twice among them included, or that break one of the server's own rules.
- [`E_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`](../errors.md#e_identity_required): the server runs with no identity.
- [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo): the server's store is not there; the server serves on.
- [`E_INTERNAL`](../errors.md#e_internal): the operation panicked, a bug.

Then the errors of the operation, as [`swarmops ref txn`](../commands/ref-txn.md#errors) lists them.
